title: Haiyuan earthquake
summary: A very large earthquake struck Haiyuan County, then part of Gansu Province in the Chinese Republic, on the evening of 16 December 1920. It produced 675 major loess landslides. A historians' account gives more than 200,000 deaths, with county-based estimates ranging from 234,117 to 314,092.

uncertainty.note: Date given by two opened pages; the DisasterHistory page gives only the evening. Aftershocks are reported to have continued for three years; they are not dated here.

importance.justification: DisasterHistory calls it the world's second deadliest earthquake of the twentieth century, and it caused widespread destruction across rural Gansu and Ningxia.
